Ashwin: heads-up — saw persistent memory growth in KV cache on canary over multi-hour long-context runs. tenant 'voicebot-prod' is holding ~72% of residency even when idle. tail latency for other tenants spikes. attaching quick flamegraph link: https://internal/fg/1749
Mia: ugh, thanks. saw that too during the 3h soak. snapshot at 2h: total_kv_pages=1.9M, resident_by_tenant={voicebot:1.37M, search-prod:220k, misc:310k} :thinking:
Leah: is this pure LRU churn or fragmentation? could be that long sessions allocate lots of small slices that don't coalesce so free lists are fragmented
Ryan: my profiling shows eviction pressure metric correlates with seq_len distribution. Long-context requests keep large KV entries pinned via hot prefixes. We currently evict on global LRU across tenants, so noisy tenant wins.
Olivia: do we have per-tenant residency metrics exposed? i.e. kv_resident_bytes{tenant}, kv_evictions{tenant}, kv_fragmentation_ratio?
Mia: we have kv_evictions_per_min but not fragmentation ratio. I ran a microbench: repeatedly extend context to 64k tokens, then stop traffic. host-level resident stays high for >45m, evictions almost 0 because LRU never ages those entries — they're reaccessed by the long-context session's KV pointers.
Ashwin: TL;DR: noisy neighbor keeps KV pages alive by keeping rev_cache pointers; global LRU doesn't prevent unfair residency. Impact: 3-5% tail latency regressions for small customers and increased memory OOM risk on packed nodes.
Leah: proposals:
- per-tenant soft residency cap (percent of node memory) + reclaim under pressure
- generational eviction: prefer cold-generation pages even if recently touched
- periodic compaction to defragment free list
- session-level sentinel to demote very long-lived contexts after inactivity window
Which are prioritized?
Ryan: +1 for per-tenant soft caps. Implementation idea: track resident_pages_per_tenant and when node_free < threshold, start selecting victims from tenants exceeding soft_cap first. If still needed, global fallback. This preserves throughput for tenants within quota.
Mia: what about reuse? some tenants legitimately need large KV (e.g., RLHF agents). Need escape hatch: per-tenant "pin budget" that can be granted via SLA or request header. We should support both soft and hard caps.
Leah: generational eviction could be simpler: keep age counter per page, when promoting to hot generation require multiple hits. When memory pressure, evict from young then cold. reduces chance long sessions monopolize by single repeated access pattern.
Olivia: fragmentation: we should add a background compactor that merges adjacent free spans every N minutes. Also expose kv_fragmentation_ratio = (allocated_bytes - contiguous_free_max)/allocated_bytes. That will help ops detect nodes at risk.
sre-bot: incident: node-gpu-13 high_mem_pressure triggered at 1749122802, mem_used=93% :warning:
Ashwin: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
on_alloc(page, tenant_id): resident[tenant_id]++
on_access(page): page.last_seen = now; page.hits++;
reclaim_loop():
  if free_pages < LOW_WM:
    candidates = tenants_exceeding_softcap() or global_LRU()
    evict(select_victims(candidates))
```
Add metric kv_resident_pages_per_tenant, kv_evictions_by_policy{tenant,policy}
```

Mia: nice. Can we also soft-evict pages by demoting their KV references (so the session can rebuild but not hold physical memory)? i.e. convert to compressed on-disk blob and reconstruct on first access — costs CPU but bounds memory.
Ryan: that's basically paging to local SSD. Feasible in Dedicated; less so on hosted due to multi-tenancy on same local NVMe. We can implement compressed swap for Dedicated nodes first.
Leah: rollout plan:
1) Add per-tenant residency metrics and fragmentation metric (observability) — 1 week
2) Implement soft-cap + eviction-by-tenant policy behind flag + test — 2 weeks
3) Add generational age logic + compactor behind flag — 2 weeks
4) Optional compressed swap for Dedicated — exploratory spike
We can A/B canary on 5% of nodes with noisy tenants.
Olivia: experiments to run:
- Synthetic: 10 tenants, 1 noisy long-context at 70% traffic — measure tail latency, evictions, resident distribution
- Real traffic: pick 3 customers who opt-in (voicebot, search, internal) and run quota policy on subset of their traffic
Capture traces, kv_eviction_reason tag, and flamegraphs pre/post.
Mia: also add regression guard: if tail latency or request error rate increases >1% after policy, rollback.
Ashwin: open question: how to set soft cap defaults? static % per node or dynamic based on tenant SLA? maybe initial default 20% per tenant, max 60% by special grant. Comments?
Ryan: dynamic might be hard; start with defaults: soft_cap = min(25%, tenant_requested*1.2) and hard_cap = min(60%, tenant_requested*2). We can refine after telemetry.
Leah: agree. Also track contended_nodes metric to avoid moving tenants unnecessarily.
Olivia: will create dashboards for kv_resident_by_tenant, fragmentation, eviction_policy_breakdown.
Mia: I'll start instrumenting today and push metric names in PR. Ashwin can you own the design doc for eviction algorithm? I'll pair on metric instrumentation.
Ashwin: yep, I'll draft the doc and include perf numbers from current canary. Let's meet tomorrow 10:30 to align on metrics + rollout. :thumbsup:
